title: Al-Khafid, the Abaser
hookLine: the Abaser, who lowers the arrogant
tomorrow: Amira gets one sentence in the caption. who does she lift up?

cards: A news page wants one photo and one name for the caption, and the name they asked for is Amira's. It was her idea. She did the sketches.

So yesterday's question is the one she's chewing on: who stands in the photo? Somewhere in the back of her mind is a story from the Qur'an about a creature who said one short sentence about himself and was lowered for it.

teach.b: When Adam is made and the angels are told to bow, Iblis refuses. His reason, in Pickthall's words: "I am better than him." Then he explains: you made me of fire, and him of mud.
Better because of what he's made of. And he is sent down. That's today's name, al-Khafid, the Abaser, who lowers the arrogant.

The Qur'an pictures the last day the same way: "Abasing (some), exalting (others)." Now the part that helps this week. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says no one with an atom's weight of pride in the heart enters the Garden.
A man asks, worried: but I like my clothes nice and my shoes nice. The Prophet, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
Pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. So pride isn't nice shoes, and it isn't doing good work and being glad about it. It's the Iblis move: I'm better than him.

teach.h: THE NOBLEST: THE BEST IN CONDUCT.
teach.b: And the Qur'an's answer to that move is about everyone: "the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct."
Not by fire or mud, family or color. One human race, measured by how it acts. The line for a friend tonight: in the Qur'an, the arrogance of Iblis was a claim about what someone was made of.

how: Muslims lower themselves in sujud, forehead to the ground, in prayer, and teachers point to the hadith on pride to separate arrogance from simply liking beautiful things.

o: the One who lets people sink into failure
the One who brings the arrogant down low
the One who hides Himself from the proud

games.q: the pride of Iblis — tap the pairs.

s: liking nice clothes is the pride the hadith warns about
Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.
Iblis refused to bow because he thought what he was made of made him better
fire, not mud: I am better than him.
in the Qur'an, nobility before Allah depends on family and color
the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct.

games.q: your team project wins, and the teacher asks you to accept the award on stage alone. it really was mostly your work. what fits today's lesson?
o: go up, and name the team; being glad of good work isn't pride.
refuse to go up at all, since any credit at all is arrogance.
go up alone and keep it simple: it really was mostly yours.
games.why: pride is looking down on people, not being glad of good work. naming the others keeps the ground level.

practice: Lower your head a little and rest your hands palms down on your thighs, the body saying I'm not above anyone. Hold that posture through the sit, and bring to mind one person you've quietly looked down on.
Let the posture do the work: not shame, just level ground.

wordCard.voice: Al-Khafid: the Abaser, who lowers the arrogant, the ones who say I am better than him.

orig.note: Arabic: the Abaser, who lowers. in the traditional list beside ar-Rafi', the Exalter.

carryVoice: Here's the line: he lowers the proud, so step down first, and gladly. Day done.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 91 (pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people; Allah is beautiful and loves beauty)

sources.q: the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct.
